text:
Maya (Support): FYI seeing a surge of customer reports complaining about 5xx / timeouts on hosted inference endpoints since ~11:20 UTC. Example: several customers get repeated 502/504 on /v1/generate and /v1/chat. Ticket IDs: TICK-4921, TICK-4924, TICK-4930. Noted X-Request-IDs: req-0a1b2c, req-0a1b2d.
inc-bot: :rotating_light: Alert if: redis-prod-1 p99 latency > 200ms for 5m — triggered at 11:22:18 UTC. Error rate spike: 4xx->5xx gateway errors increased by 280%.
Alex (SRE): looking. Can someone paste last 10s of gateway logs? What backend is failing — runtime cache, prefix-cache, memcached? Any correlation with recent deploys?
Maya (Support): attaching a trimmed customer log sample: "gateway: GET /v1/generate -> upstream error code=EAI_AGAIN backend=cache service=prefix-cache timeout=250ms status=502"
Priya (Platform Eng): we had a feature rollout earlier at 11:05 that enabled prefix/KV caching on more request paths (aimed at improving cold costs). Rollout was gradual but hit 100% at 11:12 UTC. Rolling commit: fea/prefix-cache-global. Possible causation.
Jon (Oncall): confirmed alert. Redis cluster redis-prod-1 showing increased command latency and some IO errors. memcached clusters look normal. Running quick checks now.
Alex (SRE): stack trace from gateway when backend times out:
```
ERROR runtime/cache_client.go:142 getPrefixKV: redis GET timeout after 250ms for key prefix: "pfx:session:abcd1234"
upstream: cache.rpc.call timed out
proxy: returning 502 to client
```
Maya (Support): customers report retries make it worse — many get 5xx until request passes. Root cause for customer impact needs triage + mitigation.
Jon (Oncall): repro steps for engineers:
1) curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"rwd-large","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
2) Observe repeated 502/504s with "backend=prefix-cache timeout"
3) Confirm on gateway logs: grep req-id -> backend error lines

Priya (Platform Eng): quick check of redis logs shows repeated "MISCONF Redis is configured to save RDB snapshots, but the process of writing the snapshot failed" and also "read-only slave" events around 11:16-11:24 UTC. That explains some GET failures when client tried to write TTL/prefix metadata in some paths.
Alex (SRE): noticed connection saturations from app nodes -> redis client pool exhaustion. Metrics: client_connections spiked 3x and p95 latency shot to 420ms. We also see increased CPU on one redis master node.
Maya (Support): customers impacted list compiled so far: AcmeAI (acct 442), ChatFlow (acct 993), QuerySentry (acct 1201). All reported increased 5xx rate and page escalations.
Jon (Oncall): mitigation options:
- Disable prefix/KV caching feature flag (fast), OR
- Increase redis client timeouts and pool size (less immediate), OR
- Route cache misses to cold-read path without blocking user request (requires config change)

Priya (Platform Eng): disabling prefix caching is the fastest and reversible. Advocate for flip the kill-switch and monitor.
Alex (SRE): agree. I'll flip feature-flag on console for hosted inference at org-level. Command:
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.ai/flags/prefix-cache" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"enabled":false}'
```
Proceeding in 30s.
Jon (Oncall): before flip — warn customers to expect transient errors. Maya pls post brief status update in all affected tickets.
Maya (Support): posting now. Message: "We're aware of elevated 5xx for hosted inference; engineering is disabling prefix caching as a mitigation and will update shortly. ETA ~10-15m." :thumbsup: 
Alex (SRE): done. Flipped flag at 11:41:03 UTC. Observability: redis write ops from gateway dropped by ~85% within 60s. Gateway 5xx rate trending down.
inc-bot: Incident note: mitigation action recorded — feature flag prefix-cache disabled by Alex at 11:41:03 UTC.
Priya (Platform Eng): to stop cascading retries we also temporarily bumped redis client timeout from 250ms -> 500ms and increased client pool by 20% on the gateway service. That buys time while we stabilize.
Jon (Oncall): post-mitigation checks:
- 11:43:00 check: gateway 5xx rate down to baseline. p99 latency improved but still slightly elevated.
- Confirmed no OOMs on redis master; replication lag reduced.
Maya (Support): sending customers the update: "We disabled prefix caching and applied temporary client-side timeouts. You should see successful requests now. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."
Customer (ChatFlow) (message forwarded): "Thanks — can you confirm this won't recur? Our SLAs are sensitive."
Alex (SRE): immediate next actions:
- Keep prefix-cache disabled until root cause fully investigated.
- Re-run canary with synthetic traffic and incremental rollout with strict circuit-breaker and lower write rate.
- Investigate why redis returned MISCONF / read-only — check disk, RDB snapshot fails, and persistence settings.
Priya (Platform Eng): findings so far: snapshot writes failed due to ephemeral disk pressure on one redis master during its scheduled AOF rewrite; that caused redis to set MISCONF and go read-only briefly. Our prefix-cache code attempted writes (sets + TTL) that the client library didn't gracefully degrade for, causing propagated errors. Also our feature rollout increased write traffic to that code-path beyond previous test coverage.
Jon (Oncall): suggested durable mitigations:
- Make prefix-cache write operations best-effort (non-blocking) — don't fail request on cache write failure.
- Add immediate circuit-breaker when redis returns MISCONF/IOERR to avoid repeated retries.
- Update deploy checklist: run forced persistence stress tests before feature gates to redis.
- Add alert for RDB/AOF write failures to SRE runbook (higher priority)

Maya (Support): created follow-up ticket SUPPORT-2279 to notify customers postmortem and provide timeline. Customers asked for ETA on re-enabling caching.
Priya (Platform Eng): plan for re-enable: once we patch client to treat cache writes as async fire-and-forget (non-blocking), add a dead-letter queue for failed writes, and perform a gradual canary 1% -> 5% -> 25% with thresholds. Estimated time: 2-3 working days for engineering + QA.
Alex (SRE): temporary rollback done. We'll prepare a patch to handle MISCONF gracefully and add config guardrails to rollout.
Jon (Oncall): postmortem owner: Priya. Expected draft PM postmortem within 48h. Action items assigned:
- Priya: patch client write behavior + canary plan (due 48h)
- Alex: add alerts for redis persistence failures + runbook (due 24h)
- Jon: confirm scaling plan / capacity test for redis clusters (due 72h)
- Maya: customer communication & closing support tickets (ongoing)

Priya (Platform Eng): left notes for the dev team:
```
- Make cache-write side-effects fire-and-forget
- Expose circuit-breaker that trips on MISCONF/IOERR, stops further cache writes for 1min and falls back to cold path
- Add metrics: cache_write_failures, cache_write_misconf_count
- Add e2e test that simulates disk pressure and snapshot fail to confirm degradation path
```
Maya (Support): marking thread as monitored. Will update tickets with final postmortem link when available. Thanks team. :pray:
Alex (SRE): thumbs. closing incident if no regressions in 2h.
inc-bot: Incident closed for alert redis-prod-1 at 13:30:02 UTC (mitigation applied, monitoring healthy).
